re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1112: [GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance

## Description

## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Pre-CLI: preCliContentOutputSetup.js (InputContextBundle protocol)        │
│    • fetchQuestionsToInput.js      → input/<KEY>/existing_questions.json     │
│    • fetchParentContextToInput.js  → input/<KEY>/parent_context_*.md         │
│      (linked Confluence pages converted via format:'md' /                    │
│       ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback)              │
│    • fetchConfluenceOutputContext  → input/<KEY>/confluence_output_target.json│
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_current.md│
│      (existing page via format:'md' + [[ic:REF]]...[[/ic]] anchors injected  │
│       from raw storage <ac:inline-comment-marker> elements)                  │
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_comments.*│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CLI Run: scripts/run-agent.sh                                             │
│    • Base prompts: instructions/wiki_publisher/workflow.md                   │
│                    + prompts/wiki_publisher_prompt.md                        │
│                    + instructions/common/input_context_reading.md            │
│                    + instructions/common/confluence_comments.md              │
│                    + cliPromptsByTracker.{jira,ado,github,confluence}        │
│    • Merged child prompts: project-specific skill/rule .md files             │
│    • Produces: outputs/response.md (GFM Markdown preserving [[ic:REF]])      │
│                outputs/confluence_replies.json (optional inline replies)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. Post-CLI: writeContentOutput.js + js/common/contentOutput.js              │
│    (WikiSyncContract + TrackerBridge protocol)                               │
│    • Publish replies from outputs/confluence_replies.json while anchors live │
│    • Find-or-create "<KEY> <Summary>[ — <pageTitleSuffix>]" under            │
│      contentOutput.parentPageId                                              │
│    • Stage outputs/response.md → outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md      │
│      and run confluence_sync_markdown_directory (MarkdownConfluenceSync:     │
│      MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage + InlineCommentAnchorPreserver)   │
│    • Post wiki link comment & optional field update via TrackerBridge        │
│      (trackers.createTracker: Jira / ADO / GitHub Issues)                    │
│    • Run contentOutput.thenAction OR assignForReview + postTokenUsageComments│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Named protocols & invariants:

- **`InputContextBundle` protocol (`preCliContentOutputSetup.js`)** — before the CLI starts, `input/<KEY>/` receives the work item itself, open/answered questions (`existing_questions.json`), parent/sibling context and linked wiki/Confluence pages (`fetchParentContextToInput.js`, no-op when `parentContextFetch.enabled` is false), and the existing target wiki page snapshot converted from Confluence storage to Markdown + inline comments (`fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js`). **Invariant**: every enrichment step in `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` is non-fatal; a failure in parent-context or w…

{
  "key": "gh-1112",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance",
    "description": "## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Pre-CLI: preCliContentOutputSetup.js (InputContextBundle protocol)        │
│    • fetchQuestionsToInput.js      → input/<KEY>/existing_questions.json     │
│    • fetchParentContextToInput.js  → input/<KEY>/parent_context_*.md         │
│      (linked Confluence pages converted via format:'md' /                    │
│       ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback)              │
│    • fetchConfluenceOutputContext  → input/<KEY>/confluence_output_target.json│
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_current.md│
│      (existing page via format:'md' + [[ic:REF]]...[[/ic]] anchors injected  │
│       from raw storage <ac:inline-comment-marker> elements)                  │
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_comments.*│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CLI Run: scripts/run-agent.sh                                             │
│    • Base prompts: instructions/wiki_publisher/workflow.md                   │
│                    + prompts/wiki_publisher_prompt.md                        │
│                    + instructions/common/input_context_reading.md            │
│                    + instructions/common/confluence_comments.md              │
│                    + cliPromptsByTracker.{jira,ado,github,confluence}        │
│    • Merged child prompts: project-specific skill/rule .md files             │
│    • Produces: outputs/response.md (GFM Markdown preserving [[ic:REF]])      │
│                outputs/confluence_replies.json (optional inline replies)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. Post-CLI: writeContentOutput.js + js/common/contentOutput.js              │
│    (WikiSyncContract + TrackerBridge protocol)                               │
│    • Publish replies from outputs/confluence_replies.json while anchors live │
│    • Find-or-create "<KEY> <Summary>[ — <pageTitleSuffix>]" under            │
│      contentOutput.parentPageId                                              │
│    • Stage outputs/response.md → outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md      │
│      and run confluence_sync_markdown_directory (MarkdownConfluenceSync:     │
│      MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage + InlineCommentAnchorPreserver)   │
│    • Post wiki link comment & optional field update via TrackerBridge        │
│      (trackers.createTracker: Jira / ADO / GitHub Issues)                    │
│    • Run contentOutput.thenAction OR assignForReview + postTokenUsageComments│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1112: [GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance

## Description

## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Pre-CLI: preCliContentOutputSetup.js (InputContextBundle protocol)        │
│    • fetchQuestionsToInput.js      → input/<KEY>/existing_questions.json     │
│    • fetchParentContextToInput.js  → input/<KEY>/parent_context_*.md         │
│      (linked Confluence pages converted via format:'md' /                    │
│       ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback)              │
│    • fetchConfluenceOutputContext  → input/<KEY>/confluence_output_target.json│
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_current.md│
│      (existing page via format:'md' + [[ic:REF]]...[[/ic]] anchors injected  │
│       from raw storage <ac:inline-comment-marker> elements)                  │
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_comments.*│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CLI Run: scripts/run-agent.sh                                             │
│    • Base prompts: instructions/wiki_publisher/workflow.md                   │
│                    + prompts/wiki_publisher_prompt.md                        │
│                    + instructions/common/input_context_reading.md            │
│                    + instructions/common/confluence_comments.md              │
│                    + cliPromptsByTracker.{jira,ado,github,confluence}        │
│    • Merged child prompts: project-specific skill/rule .md files             │
│    • Produces: outputs/response.md (GFM Markdown preserving [[ic:REF]])      │
│                outputs/confluence_replies.json (optional inline replies)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. Post-CLI: writeContentOutput.js + js/common/contentOutput.js              │
│    (WikiSyncContract + TrackerBridge protocol)                               │
│    • Publish replies from outputs/confluence_replies.json while anchors live │
│    • Find-or-create "<KEY> <Summary>[ — <pageTitleSuffix>]" under            │
│      contentOutput.parentPageId                                              │
│    • Stage outputs/response.md → outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md      │
│      and run confluence_sync_markdown_directory (MarkdownConfluenceSync:     │
│      MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage + InlineCommentAnchorPreserver)   │
│    • Post wiki link comment & optional field update via TrackerBridge        │
│      (trackers.createTracker: Jira / ADO / GitHub Issues)                    │
│    • Run contentOutput.thenAction OR assignForReview + postTokenUsageComments│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Named protocols & invariants:

- **`InputContextBundle` protocol (`preCliContentOutputSetup.js`)** — before the CLI starts, `input/<KEY>/` receives the work item itself, open/answered questions (`existing_questions.json`), parent/sibling context and linked wiki/Confluence pages (`fetchParentContextToInput.js`, no-op when `parentContextFetch.enabled` is false), and the existing target wiki page snapshot converted from Confluence storage to Markdown + inline comments (`fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js`). **Invariant**: every enrichment step in `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` is non-fatal; a failure in parent-context or w…

    "description": "## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)

  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1112: [GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance

## Description

## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼

    "description": "## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

# gh-1112: [GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance

## Description

## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Pre-CLI: preCliContentOutputSetup.js (InputContextBundle protocol)        │
│    • fetchQuestionsToInput.js      → input/<KEY>/existing_questions.json     │
│    • fetchParentContextToInput.js  → input/<KEY>/parent_context_*.md         │
│      (linked Confluence pages converted via format:'md' /                    │
│       ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback)              │
│    • fetchConfluenceOutputContext  → input/<KEY>/confluence_output_target.json│
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_current.md│
│      (existing page via format:'md' + [[ic:REF]]...[[/ic]] anchors injected  │
│       from raw storage <ac:inline-comment-marker> elements)                  │
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_comments.*│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CLI Run: scripts/run-agent.sh                                             │
│    • Base prompts: instructions/wiki_publisher/workflow.md                   │
│                    + prompts/wiki_publisher_prompt.md                        │
│                    + instructions/common/input_context_reading.md            │
│                    + instructions/common/confluence_comments.md              │
│                    + cliPromptsByTracker.{jira,ado,github,confluence}        │
│    • Merged child prompts: project-specific skill/rule .md files             │
│    • Produces: outputs/response.md (GFM Markdown preserving [[ic:REF]])      │
│                outputs/confluence_replies.json (optional inline replies)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. Post-CLI: writeContentOutput.js + js/common/contentOutput.js              │
│    (WikiSyncContract + TrackerBridge protocol)                               │
│    • Publish replies from outputs/confluence_replies.json while anchors live │
│    • Find-or-create "<KEY> <Summary>[ — <pageTitleSuffix>]" under            │
│      contentOutput.parentPageId                                              │
│    • Stage outputs/response.md → outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md      │
│      and run confluence_sync_markdown_directory (MarkdownConfluenceSync:     │
│      MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage + InlineCommentAnchorPreserver)   │
│    • Post wiki link comment & optional field update via TrackerBridge        │
│      (trackers.createTracker: Jira / ADO / GitHub Issues)                    │
│    • Run contentOutput.thenAction OR assignForReview + postTokenUsageComments│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Named protocols & invariants:

- **`InputContextBundle` protocol (`preCliContentOutputSetup.js`)** — before the CLI starts, `input/<KEY>/` receives the work item itself, open/answered questions (`existing_questions.json`), parent/sibling context and linked wiki/Confluence pages (`fetchParentContextToInput.js`, no-op when `parentContextFetch.enabled` is false), and the existing target wiki page snapshot converted from Confluence storage to Markdown + inline comments (`fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js`). **Invariant**: every enrichment step in `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` is non-fatal; a failure in parent-context or w…

    "summary": "[GOAL] Generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic wiki_publisher base agent — bidirectional Markdown sync via parent inheritance",
    "description": "## Goal — generic tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent (v2, renamed to `wiki_publisher` + pinned dmtools Markdown↔Confluence sync)

One sentence: **`dmtools-agents` gains a reusable, tracker- and wiki-agnostic `wiki_publisher` base agent** — any downstream project can specialize a wiki-publishing workflow (testing checklists, QA test plans, release specs, audit reports) purely through `"parent"` JSON inheritance and markdown skill composition, backed today by dmtools' bidirectional Markdown↔Confluence sync (`ConfluenceStorageMarkdown` ↔ `MarkdownConfluenceSync`).

Today `dmtools-agents` and `dmtools-core` already contain all the primitives for bidirectional Markdown ↔ Confluence round-tripping and rich ticket context ingestion:
- **Inbound (Confluence → Markdown)**: `confluence_get_children_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` and `confluence_content_by_id({ contentId, format: 'md' })` run `ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback(storageValue, exportViewValue)` in `dmtools-core`, while `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js` extracts `<ac:inline-comment-marker ac:ref="GUID">` from raw storage XHTML and injects `[[ic:GUID]]...[[/ic]]` placeholders into `input/confluence_output_current.md`.
- **Outbound (Markdown → Confluence)**: `contentOutput.publishPage` writes `outputs/response.md` to `outputs/confluence_sync_<KEY>/index.md` and calls `confluence_sync_markdown_directory`, which invokes `MarkdownConfluenceSync` + `MarkdownToConfluenceStorage.toStorage` + `InlineCommentAnchorPreserver.restoreAnchors` (`preserveInlineComments = true` by default) to convert GitHub-flavored Markdown into Confluence storage XHTML while preserving the root page's title/parent, inline comment anchors, and attachments.
- **Missing pieces**: these primitives are currently only wired inside role-specific agents (`story_description.json`, `story_acceptance_criteria.json`, `story_solution.json`), `preCliContentOutputSetup.js` omits `fetchParentContextToInput.js`, and `writeContentOutput.js` / `contentOutput.js` still call `jira_post_comment`, `jira_get_ticket`, and `jira_update_field` directly instead of routing through `js/common/trackers.js`. Landing `wiki_publisher.json` as an abstract input-to-wiki contract — with `"wiki"` / `"tracker_field"` target aliases and tracker-agnostic notifications — turns every future wiki generator into a thin `"parent"` override in the consuming repo.

## Why this framing

- **Earlier framing retracted (`confluence_publisher.json` agent name)**: naming the base agent `confluence_publisher` couples every child agent's `"parent"` path and `contextId` to Confluence. Renaming the base agent to **`wiki_publisher`** (`wiki_publisher.json`, `contextId: "wiki_publisher"`) and supporting `contentOutput.target: "wiki"` alongside `"confluence"` keeps child agent configs stable if a future wiki backend (ADO Wiki, GitHub Wiki, Notion) is introduced behind `contentOutput.js`, while using the dmtools Confluence Markdown sync engine as the default wiki implementation today.
- **Earlier framing retracted (dedicated `story_checklist.json` agent in `dmtools-agents`)**: adding a new root `*.json` agent for each artifact type (checklists, test plans, release notes) leaks domain-specific structure into the shared repository and multiplies maintenance across identical pre/post pipelines. Retracted in favor of a single abstract `wiki_publisher.json` base contract specialized via `"parent"` + `cliPrompts`.
- **Earlier framing retracted (copying external skill folders via `setupCommands` before CLI start)**: shell-copying skill directories into `.claude/skills` at runtime is unnecessary when the consuming repo's child config (or `.dmtools/config.js` `cliPrompts.wiki_publisher`) can reference skill and rule `.md` files directly in `params.cliPrompts`.
- **Tracker-agnostic by construction**: the originating work item may live in Jira, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Issues. Ticket comments, status transitions, review assignment, and optional tracker-field back-links must route through `js/common/trackers.js` (`createTracker`) and `cliPromptsByTracker`.

## Architecture

```
Consuming repo child agent (e.g. story_checklist.json)
  "parent": { "path": ".../wiki_publisher.json", "merge": ["params.cliPrompts"] }
  + project skill .md refs in params.cliPrompts
  + customParams.contentOutput: { target: "wiki" | "confluence", space, parentPageId, pageTitleSuffix }
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Pre-CLI: preCliContentOutputSetup.js (InputContextBundle protocol)        │
│    • fetchQuestionsToInput.js      → input/<KEY>/existing_questions.json     │
│    • fetchParentContextToInput.js  → input/<KEY>/parent_context_*.md         │
│      (linked Confluence pages converted via format:'md' /                    │
│       ConfluenceStorageMarkdown.toMarkdownWithRenderedFallback)              │
│    • fetchConfluenceOutputContext  → input/<KEY>/confluence_output_target.json│
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_current.md│
│      (existing page via format:'md' + [[ic:REF]]...[[/ic]] anchors injected  │
│       from raw storage <ac:inline-comment-marker> elements)                  │
│                                      input/<KEY>/confluence_output_comments.*│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CLI Run: scripts/run-agent.sh                                             │
│    • Base prompts: instructions/wiki_publisher/workflow.md                   │
│                    + prompts/wiki_publisher_prompt.md                        │
│                    + instructions/common/input_context_reading.md            │
│                    + instructions/common/confluence_comments.md              │
│                    + cliPromptsByTracker.{jira,ado,github,confluence}        │
│    • Merged child prompts: project-specific skill/rule .md files             │
│    • Produces: outputs/response.md (GFM Markdown preserving [[ic:REF]])      │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

│    • Publish replies from outputs/confluence_replies.json while anchors live │
│    • Find-or-create "<KEY> <Summary>[ — <pageTitleSuffix>]" under            │
│      contentOutput.parentPageId                                              │

│      and run confluence_sync_markdown_directory (MarkdownConfluenceSync:     │

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
